subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence.

Right now, __my hands are full.__
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given phrase** "my hands are full" **is an idiom in English that means being very busy.

 
 
• **Example:** I cannot take on another project right now; my hands are full with the current assignments.
 
 

Therefore, the **correct answer **is **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** "My hands are filled up" can confuse with the literal filling of hands but does not convey the idiomatic meaning of being busy.
 
• **Option 2 **"My hands are swollen" suggests a physical condition, not busyness.
 
• **Option 3** "I'm very tired" indicates fatigue, which is different from being busy
